name: Squarepusher
editorial_article:
Squarepusher is the primary recording alias of Thomas Russell Jenkinson, an English multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and bass virtuoso who emerged as a defining force in the mid-1990s electronic scene. Born in Chelmsford, Essex, Jenkinson bridged the gap between the frantic, cut-and-paste aesthetics of drill and bass and the intricate, harmonic complexities of jazz fusion. His sound is instantly recognizable, characterized by lightning-fast, hyper-processed breakbeats layered against his own sophisticated, jazz-inflected bass guitar work, often processed through complex digital signal paths.

He first gained prominence in the fertile underground electronic circuit of the mid-90s, with early support from Richard D. James (Aphex Twin), who helped facilitate his debut long-player, 'Feed Me Weird Things' (1996), on the Rephlex label. Jenkinson quickly moved to Warp Records, cementing his status as a key figure in the "Intelligent Dance Music" (IDM) movement. Across a career spanning over three decades, Squarepusher has consistently experimented with the boundaries of electronic music, moving from his early frenetic jungle-inspired roots to the more electro-acoustic, abstract, and highly programmed soundscapes of later albums like 'Go Plastic' and the visual-audio synthesis of 'Ufabulum'. His brother, Andy Jenkinson, is also a notable electronic musician known as Ceephax Acid Crew. Throughout his career, Squarepusher has remained a restless innovator, constantly balancing the raw, physical virtuosity of his live playing with the cold, precise possibilities of digital synthesis. By blending these disparate elements, he created a signature style that continues to influence the landscape of electronic music.
editorial_bio: Squarepusher is the alias of electronic virtuoso Tom Jenkinson, celebrated for his complex fusion of high-speed drill and bass with intricate jazz-inflected bass guitar performance. A key fixture of the Warp Records roster, he remains a central figure in the evolution of IDM and breakbeat-focused electronic music.
